text:
Matthew Knies got his night. The former Maple Leaf went back to Toronto on Saturday, and the Blue Jackets came back for a 4-3 win, with Zach Werenski scoring the winner, per Reuters. Adam Fantilli had called the previous meeting with the Leafs "an embarrassing game for us," as TSN's headline put it, so this one meant something. Then came Monday in New Jersey: a 3-2 loss, and Mathieu Olivier leaving with an upper-body injury, per Daily Faceoff.

That is the Columbus season in two games. At 9-13-0, the Blue Jackets have about three points fewer than their play has earned by our standings model, but that isn't enough to change the picture. They have 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and they have scored about nine and a half fewer goals than those chances predict.

Werenski is the constant. He has 11 points in his last 10 games, set another franchise record in Toronto (per Yahoo Sports), and his pair with Damon Severson has outscored teams 19-9 at 5-on-5 on an even share of the chances. CBS Sports says Cam Talbot is channeling his best 20-something season. The Charlie Coyle, Olivier and Cole Sillinger line has been the best forward group by chances (53%), which is why Olivier's injury matters.

Our playoff odds have Columbus at 8%. What we'd watch: whether the shooters finally catch up to their chances, and how long Olivier is out.
headline: Knies gets his night, Columbus still can't finish
